openQuestions.text: What exact order API endpoints and operations are in scope beyond the named operations (placement, retrieval, read, update, delete)?
What are the exact standardized unauthorized response format and status/body requirements?
What status code and response body should be returned for authorization denials?
Which specific roles are authorized to access audit logs?
Is there an existing audit API and/or audit UI, or must one be built as part of this feature?
Are audit records required for order delete actions in addition to create, update, and read?
What exact authentication attempt details must be logged for every API request?
What exact performance threshold defines "acceptable performance" for audit-log filtering? Is the success metric of under 1 second for large logs contractual?
What exact date-range format and timezone handling rules apply to audit-log filtering?
What exact output shape is required for audit-log retrieval responses?
Is secure export of audit records in scope for this feature, and if so, what formats are required?
What is the required retention period for audit log records themselves?
Which order-related sensitive fields, besides payment credentials, must be masked or omitted from logs?
Does this feature require support for token revocation and refresh behavior at validation time, or is that outside scope?
Which service within the monolith owns the audit-log storage and access policy as Information Owner/Custodian?
Does this feature trigger DPIA review/update under SOS-47951 for affected in-scope products and data flows?

userStories.title: As a Compliance Auditor, I want immutable audit records for order actions so that online food order activity can be reviewed and reconciled
As a Platform Security Administrator, I want authenticated access enforced on order APIs so that online food orders are placed only by trusted consumers
As a Platform Security Administrator, I want object-level authorization on order resources so that consumers can access only their own food orders

openQuestions.text: What are the exact API endpoint paths, HTTP methods, request schemas, response schemas, and status codes for:
order submission,
manager status retrieval,
customer status retrieval,
status update?
What exact order fields make up “customer info”?
What exact item identifiers and menu/inventory reference fields are required for order submission?
What are the complete allowed order status values and exact transition matrix?
Are `received`, `preparing`, `ready`, and `delivered` the full status set or examples only?
Is there a cancellation status or failure status in scope?
What exact authentication mechanism is required for customers and managers?
What exact authorization model determines manager permissions and scope boundaries?
Can managers update any order in the system or only orders for a restaurant/location they manage?
What exact idempotency contract is required for repeated submissions?
How should the system behave if menu API or inventory API is unavailable at submission time?
If menu and inventory systems return conflicting availability information, which system is authoritative?
Is estimated delivery or pickup time mandatory for every customer status response, or only when available?
What format makes status information “clear” for response consumers?
What are the exact error response shapes and standard error codes/messages?
What rate limits apply to status APIs?
What notification channels are in scope for “relevant staff” notifications?
Who qualifies as “relevant staff” for each status change?
What is the required behavior if notification dispatch fails after a successful status update?
Are notification delivery attempts required to be persisted or only dispatched?
What is the required retention period for order records, audit logs, and notification logs beyond the 30-day retrievability success metric and 5-year policy documentation requirement?
Does this feature require DPIA review under SOS-47951 due to customer data flow changes?
What data classification level applies to each order/customer field?
Are there specific response format standards, versioning rules, or API compatibility conventions for this monolith service?

userStories.title: As a Customer, I want to view the current status of my food order so that I can know when to expect delivery or pickup
As a Restaurant Manager, I want to track the processing state of orders so that I can manage kitchen workflow efficiently
As a Customer, I want to place an online food order so that I can conveniently purchase meals from the app
